article_lead.description: an ordered-data cutoff that locates a chosen fraction of a sample and summarizes its centre, spread or tails

new_bank_questions.title: A percentile between observations
new_bank_questions.body: The ordered sample is 1, 3, 5, 9, 12. Find its p=0.6 quantile by (a) the empirical-CDF inverse and (b) R's type-7 interpolation rule. Explain why they differ.
new_bank_questions.answer: The empirical inverse uses index ceil(5×0.6)=3 and gives x_(3)=5. Type 7 uses h=1+(5−1)×0.6=3.4, so it interpolates 40% from x_(3)=5 to x_(4)=9, giving 5+0.4(9−5)=6.6. The empirical CDF is a step function, whereas type 7 fills the gap between adjacent order statistics.

new_bank_questions.title: A quartile with tied observations
new_bank_questions.body: The ordered sample is 2, 2, 2, 9. Find the 0.75 quantile by the empirical-CDF inverse and by R's type-7 rule. What does the difference show?
new_bank_questions.answer: The empirical inverse uses ceil(4×0.75)=3 and returns x_(3)=2: three of four values are already at most 2. Type 7 uses h=1+3×0.75=3.25 and returns 2+0.25(9−2)=3.75. Interpolation can put a reported quantile where no value was observed, especially when a large CDF jump from ties sits beside a gap.
